g3ela-24-1-teach-morph: [curious] What do a letter, a story, and a grocery list have in common? Somebody wrote them! There's a root that means write, and it has two spellings. Script. And scribe. Here's a word that's not on your list. Postscript. Post means after. So a postscript is writing you add after a letter: P.S.! Read the four words and think about the questions. Then tap See if you cracked it, and type the missing parts.
g3ela-24-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Battlements. Here's a sentence. The archers hid behind the battlements at the top of the wall. They hid behind them, up on top of the wall. So battlements must be the bumpy stone edge on top of a castle wall. One, read the sentence. Two, look for word parts. Three, check that the meaning fits. Now fill in each sentence from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Then play the matching game.
g3ela-24-1-teach-gram: [warmly] Think of a paragraph like a table. The main idea is the tabletop. The details are the legs that hold it up. Listen. Knights trained hard. They practiced with swords. They rode horses every day. Knights trained hard is the main idea. The other two hold it up. And I like pizza? That's off the topic. Read the paragraph, and tap Now check your thinking. Then sort each sentence: main idea, detail, or off the topic.
g3ela-24-1-teach-spell: Say these with me. Painful. Painless. Same base word: pain. Ful means full of, so painful is full of pain. Less means without. Now two more jobs. Calm, calmness. Ness turns a describing word into a thing. Calm, calmly. Ly tells how something was done. Say the words in Group A and Group B, and tap See the Rule. Then sort all eight words.
g3ela-24-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Script and scribe mean write, so look for them. Scriptwriter. A scriptwriter writes the words actors say in a movie. Script, writing. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-24-2-teach-vocab: Ever seen a joust? Two knights charge at each other on horseback, each holding a long wooden lance. Lance. They charge holding it, so a lance must be a long pole for fighting on a horse. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-24-2-teach-gram: Which one holds up the others? Bakers made bread. The castle kitchen was busy. Cooks roasted meat. It's the middle one! The kitchen was busy, and the other two show how. Read the Remember box. Then in each mixed-up paragraph, tap the main idea.
g3ela-24-2-teach-spell: Be a suffix detective. Which word means without? Mindful. Breathless. Fondness. Softly. Breathless! Breath, plus less: without breath. Read the rule. Then in each row, tap the one word with the ending named above it.
g3ela-24-2-teach-rwm: [warmly] Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from today's article. In reality, not every knight followed the code. Part one, read like a reader. Some knights broke the rules of chivalry. Part two, read like a writer. It's short, and In reality warns you a surprise is coming: the truth, not the story. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: In reality, not every owl stays up all night. Now it's your turn with the sentence about years of training. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-24-3-teach-morph: Let's snap three parts together, like blocks. De. Script. Ion. Description! A description writes down what something is like. Say the parts out loud, then say them fast as one word. Type the whole word in each box, and tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-24-3-teach-vocab: Listen for this word in a busy town. Stall. A merchant sold apples from his stall in the market square. He sold things from it, outside, so a stall must be a little shop with a table. Put a bank word in each blank. If the sentence makes sense, keep it. Then try the matching game.
g3ela-24-3-teach-gram: Three details, one topic. Smiths made tools. Weavers made cloth. Potters made bowls. What one word are they all about? Workers! That one word is the topic. Read the Remember box. Then read each set of details, and type the one word they're about.
g3ela-24-3-teach-spell: Oops! I split gladness like this: gladn, ess. That's not right. The base word is glad. So it breaks into glad, and ness. Glad is a describing word, and ness turns it into a thing. Read the rule. Then tap each card to break the word apart.
g3ela-24-4-teach-morph: Eyes closed for a second. What do script and scribe mean? Write! Keep that in your head. Here's a word that's not on the dice. Subscription. You write your name to sign up. Now tap Roll the Dice. Say what each word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.
g3ela-24-4-teach-vocab: Today's article talks about legends. A legend is an old story people told for years, like the stories of King Arthur. Did it really happen? Nobody knows for sure. Try each bank word in a blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Then finish with the matching game.
g3ela-24-4-teach-gram: One of these wandered off. The market was busy. People bought fish. My cat is orange. Which one? My cat is orange! It isn't about the market. In each paragraph, tap the sentence that's off the topic. If every sentence fits, tap No mistake.
g3ela-24-4-teach-spell: Here's my roll. Thought. Do I want full of thought? Then I pick ful: thoughtful. Without thought? Less: thoughtless. I choose the ending that does the job I need. Tap Roll the dice, pick an ending, and say why. Then tap Check my answer.
